{{Short description|Swedish experimental psychologist}}
'''Dr. Johan N. Lundström''' (born 1973) is a Swedish [[biologist]] and [[psychologist]].<ref>Lundström, J.N. (2001). Review of: Psychophysiological recording, 2nd edn. by Stern et al. Scandinavian journal of behaviour therapy, 30(4), 202-203.</ref>

He was awarded his Ph.D. in 2005 from [[Uppsala University]]<ref>Johan N. Lundström: ''Human pheromones : psychological and neurological modulation of a putative human pheromone'', Diss., Uppsala, 2005. [http://libris.kb.se/bib/9968560 Libris record]</ref> and is most notable for his [[chemosensory]] work,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.thesmartset.com/article/article06030801.aspx|title = The Sweet Smell of Species Success}}</ref> and currently works at karalinska insetutet      

His experiments involve the use of [[neuroimaging]] and testing of human behaviour. Johan Lundström's Group of the department of clinical neuroscience currently conduct basic research into the understanding of the neural and behavioural function of the [[olfactory system]] and how it interacts with other senses to understand our environment in [[health]] and disease.
